title: Multi-year financial plan
idea: Which combination of revenue and cost actions keeps the operating plan viable?
outline: Decision and planning horizon; base trajectory without action; pressures by driver; opportunity portfolio; timing, ownership and decisions.
exhibit: Plot annual resources under the baseline and feasible action cases; follow with a lever table showing timing, value basis and delivery dependencies.
depth: Explain structural versus temporary gaps, restrictions on funding, overlaps between levers and downside cases. Never call a sized opportunity a booked saving.

title: Statement of work and change order
idea: Exactly what changes, what stays fixed, and what must the sponsor accept?
outline: Mandate or existing scope; requested change; deliverables and acceptance; client inputs, capacity and timetable; commercial impact and sign-off.
exhibit: A before/change/after matrix with deliverable, owner, due date, acceptance test and fee impact.
depth: Distinguish a net-new SOW from an amendment. Identify exclusions and dependencies. Do not infer contract terms, rates or authority to sign.

title: Independent benefits realization review
idea: How much of the announced benefit is supported, and what remains unproven?
outline: Claim tested; baseline and period; validation method; supported, unsupported and disputed amounts; management response and action.
exhibit: Claim-to-actual schedule by initiative: original estimate, comparable actual, adjustments, support and disposition.
depth: Separate cash reduction, cost avoidance and timing. Disclose attribution limits; distinguish the independent auditor's finding from management's response. The exemplar is the NYC Comptroller's audit, not a BCG audit.

title: Support-function redesign
idea: What should central teams change so frontline staff get better service?
outline: Service problem; root causes and demand; design choices by function; changed accountabilities; transition and issue resolution.
exhibit: Before-and-after handoff for one service, followed by initiative cards with owner, service outcome and execution risk.
depth: Show who gains or loses decision rights, how work moves and how service continuity is protected. Separate proposed design from implemented change.

title: Line-by-line expenditure review
idea: Which spending pressures require intervention rather than an across-the-board cut?
outline: Scope and expenditure perimeter; historical composition and growth; pressure drivers; intervention choices; phased implementation.
exhibit: An expenditure bridge or trend by spending type, paired with a prioritized list of interventions.
depth: Distinguish direct operating spend from transfers, nominal growth from volume effects, and a policy choice from an efficiency. State where comparability ends.

title: Fiscal performance diagnostic
idea: Which opportunities warrant detailed diligence in the next phase?
outline: Mandate and scope; fiscal baseline; comparative diagnostics; opportunity inventory; shortlist and next-phase tests.
exhibit: A screening register with responsible function, opportunity, timing, potential impact and evidence still needed.
depth: Describe screening versus validation. Do not aggregate unvalidated overlaps or present a long list as an implementable savings commitment.

title: Committee service profiles
idea: Which level of service is required and what discretion does the committee have?
outline: Repeat one card per service: purpose and recipients; cost basis; mandate; service level and rationale; alternatives and consequences.
exhibit: Comparable service cards with a mandate/level assessment and an options-versus-implications table.
depth: Keep legal obligation separate from the chosen service level. Show the trade-off for users, budget and deliverability; do not imply that discretionary means unnecessary.

title: Core service portfolio review
idea: Where should leaders investigate service changes, and which decisions are outside scope?
outline: Mandate; service inventory; core-service and service-level filters; portfolio findings; decisions and limits.
exhibit: A classification matrix with explicit criteria, illustrated by one service profile and the implications of changing it.
depth: Separate the enterprise readout from committee detail. Peer comparisons raise questions; they do not establish legal discretion or automatically justify cuts.

title: Detailed options appraisal
idea: Which structural option performs best against the decision criteria, and when would that choice change?
outline: Decision and constraints; longlist and shortlist; comparable options; financial and non-financial impacts; transition risks and decision.
exhibit: A side-by-side option matrix with common assumptions and a separate view of one-off transition cost, recurring benefit and payback.
depth: Explain the counterfactual and non-financial trade-offs. Identify the assumption most likely to change the ranking; do not claim consensus without evidence.

title: Board summary of an options decision
idea: What decision can the board take today without reading the technical appraisal?
outline: Decision requested; options retained; criteria that distinguish them; practical consequences; unresolved issue and next decision.
exhibit: One compact comparison using the same option names and measures as the detailed appraisal.
depth: Keep residual uncertainty visible. Reference the technical analysis instead of repeating it; where no option has been endorsed, request a decision rather than inventing one.

title: Operating model and investment portfolio
idea: Which activities belong centrally, locally or in shared services, and what should be funded first?
outline: Service outcomes; current delivery constraints; proposed allocation of work and decision rights; functional cases; dependencies and sequencing.
exhibit: Responsibility map by activity plus a portfolio table pointing to individual cases, transition costs and assumptions.
depth: Show a real handoff and escalation path. Account for retained local work, transition effort and double counting across initiatives.

title: RFP proposal response
idea: Can the buyer see exactly how the proposed team will meet the requirement?
outline: Understanding of buyer outcomes; response by requirement; approach and work packages; staffing, governance, dependencies and commercial qualifications.
exhibit: Requirement-to-response matrix linked to named deliverables and acceptance points.
depth: Explain why each work package exists. Use only authorized credentials, references and pricing; do not transplant the exemplar's team or proprietary tools.

title: Sourcing and procurement business case
idea: Which categories should go to market, in which waves, and what conditions make the case worthwhile?
outline: Decision; addressable spend baseline; category opportunities; sourcing waves; implementation and run costs; benefits and mobilization.
exhibit: A wave plan beside a year-by-year case separating expense, adoption, saving and investment.
depth: Exclude non-addressable and overlapping spend. Explicitly model implementation timing, adoption and downside; approval to source is not realized savings.

title: Rapid financial-impact assessment
idea: How exposed are we this year if the shock persists, and what should management do before the next forecast?
outline: As-of date and decision horizon; pre-shock baseline; exposure by revenue stream; contrasting recovery paths; immediate management triggers.
exhibit: Observed-versus-baseline trajectory coupled with a revenue bridge separating usage, other revenues and external funding.
depth: State what was observed versus assumed. Historical analogues are not proof of recovery speed; identify the evidence that would force a reforecast.

title: Forecast vintage and methodology guide
idea: Why did successive forecasts change, and which series can readers legitimately compare?
outline: Purpose and intended uses; forecast vintages; base-period definition; coverage and frequency; assumptions changed; comparability and limitations.
exhibit: A version matrix: forecast date, data cutoff, series coverage, scenario meaning and what changed from the previous issue.
depth: Distinguish forecast vintages from actual periods and changes of scope from changes in outlook. Do not splice incompatible forecasts. Treat the overview as a dataset guide, not a separate consulting forecast.

title: Multi-year demand and revenue scenarios
idea: How do plausible changes in customer behavior translate into a revenue range and a management response?
outline: Decision and forecast date; actuals to date; distinct scenario narratives; driver assumptions; demand by segment; revenue consequences and triggers.
exhibit: Actuals joined to scenario paths at a marked cutoff, then a driver bridge from current demand to the terminal scenario.
depth: Hold units and denominators constant; separate demand from realized yield. Present scenarios as conditional paths, not probabilities, targets or established future outcomes.
